title: The first stethoscope, in 1816, was a rolled-up bundle of paper
body: At the time, doctors listened to the heart by pressing an ear straight onto the patient's chest. In 1816 at the Hôpital Necker in Paris, René Laennec was examining a young woman with signs of heart disease, and her age and sex made that, as he put it, inadmissible. He remembered how clearly the scratch of a pin travels along a piece of wood, so he rolled a quire of paper into a tube and held one end to her chest. He heard her heart more clearly than ever before, then built a **wooden tube 25 cm long** and named it the stethoscope.

cover.alt: One of Laennec's original stethoscopes: a straight wooden tube, partly wrapped in a handwritten paper label, on a teal cloth

slides.text: I rolled a quire of paper into a kind of cylinder and applied one end of it to the region of the heart and the other to my ear.
slides.attribution: René Laennec, On Mediate Auscultation (1819), in translation

slides.heading: From a paper roll to a medical tool

steps.label: A pin scratch carries along a piece of wood
A hollow wooden tube, 25 cm by 2.5 cm
A refined design in three detachable parts

slides.clue: Laennec called his method 'mediate ...', meaning listening to the body through an instrument
slides.detail: Auscultation means listening to the sounds inside the body. The word stethoscope comes from the Greek for chest and examination.

events.text: Invents the stethoscope at the Hôpital Necker
Publishes his book on mediate auscultation

slides.question: Laennec studied lung disease closely. What did he die of in 1826?
slides.explanation: He died of tuberculosis, the lung disease he had studied, and his nephew is said to have diagnosed it with a stethoscope.
